This points to a soil-borne pathogen causing whole-plant decline. Top candidates: Sudden_death_syndrome, Phytophthora, Charcoal_Rot, Brown_Stem_Rot, Fusarium.

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with the most likely:
This Phytophthora reference matches well — dying plants surrounded by healthy ones. Let me check more candidates.

I've now covered 16 classes. Let me assess:

**Test image key features:**
- Whole plant view — one plant severely wilting/dying, leaves yellowing and browning
- Surrounding plants are healthy and green
- Mature plant with pods visible on stems
- Localized collapse pattern

**Reference image comparison:**
- **Phytophthora** (whole_plant): Best match — shows dying/wilting plants surrounded by healthy green plants, same localized collapse pattern in field
- **Charcoal_Rot** (whole_plant): Similar dead/dry plants but more completely collapsed and desiccated
- **Sudden_death_syndrome** (whole_plant): Broader field yellowing pattern, less similar
- **Fusarium** (whole_plant): Plants mostly still green/upright, doesn't match
- **Soybean_Cyst_Nematode** (whole_plant): Stunted/yellowing but not dying like test image
- **Soybean_rust** (whole_plant): Defoliation without this wilting pattern
- All leaf-focused references (Bacterial_Blight, Cercospora, Downy_mildew, Frogeye, etc.) are clearly close-up leaf shots — not consistent with the test image

The Phytophthora whole-plant reference (Soybean_Dise_24.jpg) most closely matches the test image: dying plants collapsing while surrounded by healthy green neighbors, with a mix of yellow and brown leaves.
